review.source_delta: Compared v1 and v2 external source trees: exactly one path differs, crates/termrock-visibility-tests/tests/deferred.rs. The supplied patch changes only DeferredFixture::trace().
review.trace_semantics: A successful read is parsed as before. ErrorKind::NotFound returns an empty trace; every other I/O error still panics. This matches the synthetic-fixture contract: the trace file is created by the fake tool when a probe is invoked, so an absent file records no probe. Existing tests that require list/run traces assert a matching row or wait for the trace; the two invalid-input controls explicitly require an empty trace.
review.prior_failure: Inspected the pinned v1 actual stdout events and source assertions. Both tests reached the final trace check after asserting CLI exit 2, blocked result, zero executions, and null tool-version data; both failed only because read(trace_path) returned NotFound. The observed failure is a fixture accessor mismatch, not a production expectation failure.
review.runner_delta: Compared v1 and v2 runners: the only code change is the expected runplan schema version v3→v4. Runplan v4 updates paths and digest pins for the external v2 source/runner and retains the same 29-name filter and execution controls.
review.selection_and_scope: The runner parses the pinned source's #[test] declarations and requires exact order/equality with the 29-name manifest and runplan filter. It selects only the Rust deferred integration-test target, with locked/offline execution, 2 build jobs, 1 test thread, retries 0, no-fail-fast, and --run-ignored all; the exact source has zero ignored controls. No standalone Python test driver, product-control test target, or PTY journey is selected. Fixture-driven production CLI invocations inside the Rust control tests are part of this harness lane.
review.cache_and_bounds: Runplan v4 binds the v7 cache manifest, 32 locked registry packages, their archive/index hashes, sparse-index config, and lock hash. The prepared runtime preflight records successful source/tool/environment/cache checks, bounded process-group supervision (600s, TERM 5s, post-KILL 1s), and the 16 MiB combined output cap. Preflight receipt reports no Cargo spawn.
